title: Bart Scott says ESPN chose worst possible time to tell him he lost his job
description: Ryan Clark headlined ESPN’s first round of summer layoffs because ESPN chose to inform him by pulling him off the air from NFL Live on July 20. Bart Scott was also part of the layoffs, but he flew relatively under the radar, even though ESPN apparently informed him in a similarly ruthless way. “Hey, man,…
fullText:
Ryan Clark headlined ESPN's first round of summer layoffs because ESPN chose to inform him by pulling him off the air from NFL Live on July 20. Bart Scott was also part of the layoffs, but he flew relatively under the radar, even though ESPN apparently informed him in a similarly ruthless way.

"Hey, man, I was going into my radio show, and they called me, like, 'Hey, uh, just to let you know, wish we could do it in person,'" Scott said while appearing on The Joint Venture Show with Craig Carton and Lil Wayne this week. "Like, no, you don't, motherf*cker. 'Oh, I wish I could do it in person!' Nah. So, it's like, 'We're not gonna renew you.' My contract is expiring in September. So, I found out that way."

Despite the lack of respect, Scott explained why he didn't let the nature of his exit tarnish his entire tenure or his outlook on his future.

"It's part of the business," Scott said. "You understand the balance, and I don't know what they had to do when they had to trim the fat. I had never been there, where my contract was expiring, because usually when it's a year, I get renewed. But it's what it is, man. Sometimes, losing your job can be some of the biggest blessings because it forces you to try and do something else and, sometimes, step out of your comfort zone.

"Listen, one thing that is constant is change, and I've been fired before. I understand the process, and I hold no ill will. I don't even know who made the call. But I did enjoy my time there. I enjoyed using the platform, keeping myself relevant. I wasn't a first-round draft pick; I'm not a Hall of Famer. I think I was a pretty good player, but I just appreciate them giving me the platform, and I'm not gonna hold any ill will toward them. It's my job to make them regret it."

Scott entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent, signing with the Baltimore Ravens in 2002. He became an impact linebacker with the Ravens (2002-08) and New York Jets (2009-2012). After retiring, Scott joined CBS Sports' NFL Today studio crew as an analyst. With Carton and Lil Wayne, Scott cited that experience as a precursor to understanding ESPN's decision to move on.

"I thought I was going to be able to work with Shannon [Sharpe]," Scott said. "But, sometimes, in this business — at least back then — they want shows to look a certain way."

"White?" Carton bluntly posited.

"Yeah, you can't have too many of us," Scott said. "Me and Shannon are similar. We represent a certain type of demographic. We're both funny, loud, loquacious, all that type of stuff, and I never got the opportunity."

Scott joined ESPN in a limited capacity on The Michael Kay Show on ESPN 98.7 in 2017, eventually becoming a full-time personality across ESPN platforms in 2020. He most recently co-hosted Bart & Carlin on ESPN New York and appeared on ESPN's Get Up! and First Take.

title: Rangers to Open Three-Game Series With A's in Sacramento
description: The Texas Rangers head to Sacramento where they open a three-game series with the Athletics on Friday night at Sutter Health Park.
fullText:
If the Texas Rangers' backs aren't yet against the wall, they have to be at least getting somewhat close.

Texas is now two games under .500 at 60-62 after losing three of four to the last-place Los Angeles Angels.

Now, the Rangers will remain in the state of California as they travel to Sacramento, Calif., to take on the Athletics in a three-game series.

First pitch in Friday night's series opener is scheduled for 8:40 p.m. CST in another late West Coast showdown.

CW33 will have all the action on Friday night as part of their package of select Rangers Friday broadcasts. 105.3 The Fan will have the call on the radio side of things.

Kumar Rocker will take the mound for the Rangers to make his 23rd appearance (21st) start of the season.

Coming into play, Rocker is 4-9 with a 4.46 ERA, a 1.38 WHIP, and 103 strikeouts in 111 innings pitched.

In his last start against the Baltimore Orioles, Rocker struggled, allowing six earned runs in just three innings of work.

On Friday, Rocker will look to bounce back against an A's team that he has faced twice already this season.

In each of those starts, Rocker allowed just two runs, throwing 4.2 innings in Sacramento and six innings in Arlington. The Rangers lost both of those games.

At the time of this writing, the A's starting pitcher is still listed as TBD, but whoever it is, Texas will certainly need to swing the bats better than they did in the series against the Angels.

Texas scored just eight runs in the four-game set with Los Angeles and was shut out in Thursday night's series finale.

Those struggles weren't for a lack of chances, as the Rangers were able to generate multiple scoring opportunities throughout the series, but in large part were not able to capitalize after a tough series from multiple key offensive contributors.

Coming into play on Friday, Texas is outside of postseason position, trailing the American League West leaders by two games and the AL's final Wild Card spot by just a half game.

If the Rangers aren't able to get results from this series against the Athletics, it will mark a very disappointing road trip against the division's two worst teams.

The trip seemed like the golden opportunity for Texas to go on a run, but unless they find success in California's capital, they could be in some trouble.

The Baltimore Orioles have been up-and-down for much of the 2026 season, but the team have done enough to hang around in the Wild Card race, and now, they'll look for a strong seven weeks to finish their campaign on the right note.

It's not going to be easy for this team to book a spot in the post-season given how crowded the playoff race is in the American League, but with a good run home, they could shock the baseball world. Their run home continues on Friday as they begin a series with the division rival Tampa Bay Rays, and after making a shock change on star slugger Pete Alonso, he's addressed his new position in the lineup.

GettyPete Alonso of the Baltimore Orioles.

For the first time in his Major League Baseball career, Pete Alonso will hit in the leadoff spot against the Rays, and given his power, it's not a position that he would have ever expected to find himself in.

However, the Oriole clearly value what he can give them, so giving him the most amount of at bats as possible makes plenty of sense, and it's something that other teams have started to do in recent years. The most obvious example of that is with the Philadelphia Phillies and Kyle Schwarber, so when addressing the move in the lineup, Alonso naturally compared himself to the Phillies All-Star.

"I'm not saying me and him are the same guy, but I'm, like, Schwarber-adjacent," Alonso said. "I can be the right-handed Schwarber, why not?"

Traditionally, the leadoff spot in baseball was for the quickest player that could make an impact on the base paths when they get on, but in recent years, that trend has started to change, and now we see more and more home run threats hitting in that spot.

However, with a .259 average, an .833 OPS and 26 home runs, Alonso leads the Orioles in all three categories, meaning that while his power remains his biggest threat, Alonso has been getting on base as much as anyone on the team, so this threat at the top of the lineup could help Balti

Only time will tell if this move for Alonso is permanent, but given how much he's valued in the middle of the lineup, if he can come anywhere close to Schwarber's impact with the bat in the leadoff spot, this could turn out to be a move that positively effects the Orioles chances in a big way throughout the remainder of 2026.

title: Feagin, Abney all about growth in tight end room
description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. (WCIA) – No one on Illinois football’s 2026 team has score more touchdowns in an Illini uniform than Kaden Feagin. The rising senior has found the end zone 15 times through his first three years of college ball, 12 on the ground and three receiving. Aidan Laughery has the second most with eight. […]
fullText:
CHAMPAIGN, Ill. (WCIA) - No one on Illinois football's 2026 team has score more touchdowns in an Illini uniform than Kaden Feagin.

The rising senior has found the end zone 15 times through his first three years of college ball, 12 on the ground and three receiving. Aidan Laughery has the second most with eight.

Now, the Arthur, Ill. native makes the move from running back to tight end for the 2026 season. Instead of boasting an ego for his several touchdowns and more than 1,500 all-purpose yards, Feagin asked for criticism from his peers when joining the tight end room.

"All the tight ends were working after a lift and I'm like 'Hey, Christian, if you see me doing anything wrong you can tell me. It's not going to make me mad or anything. Be hard on me, be critical,'" Feagin said.

Christian Abney is a fellow-senior in the tight end room, with the difference being he has been playing that position throughout his college career. Abney played two seasons at Ball State before joining the Illini prior to the 2025 season.

Feagin says new Illini tight ends coach Jared Elliott, who coached Abney at Ball State in 2024 before working with New Mexico in 2025, has helped cultivate a tight-knit, eager to learn position group.

"I feel like all the guys, we could go up to each other and be like 'Hey, you did this wrong, you did that wrong.' But it's just all out of love," Feagin said.

Abney says Feagin's open invitation for helpful feedback opened the door for him to be honest and insightful as the ALAH grad joined the TE room.

"It really just shows his humility," Abney said. "Someone who has played that much good football over the years, and has done so well at one position, and wants to come to another one. He is going to be great at it because of his humility, and because of his ability to improve at things and realize what he needs to improve on. Him saying something like that is just a testament to how he goes about his business, and the type of person he is."

Feagin also says the tight end room has made it a priority to connect older and younger players together. Davin Stoffel is another veteran in the room who has played a fair amount of football, coming to the Illini before the 2025 season after two years at South Dakota State.

Notably, all three of the seniors listed about would seemingly be eligible, if interested, for a fifth year of eligibility under the NCAA's new rule allowing athletes to compete in five seasons across five years.

title: How Many National TV Games Will Timberwolves Have This Season?
description: The Timberwolves have a big national spotlight next season.
fullText:
The Minnesota Timberwolves should have one of the most exciting teams to watch in the NBA next season between the continued rise of Anthony Edwards, the addition of LaMelo Ball, the dominant defense of Rudy Gobert and Ayo Dosunmu and Jaden McDaniels to round things out.

They were already one of the most exciting teams to watch last season with their thrilling offense and scrappy, never-say-die attitude, something that helped them upset the Denver Nuggets in the first round of the playoffs last season, and adding Ball alone should bump that excitement up another level.

All in all, Minnesota should be must-see TV no matter who lines up on the other end of the court, and clearly the NBA agrees.

The NBA's full schedule has been released, including the slate of nationally televised games for each team, and the Timberwolves have one of the biggest pieces of the national slate in the entire league.

The Timberwolves will have 27 nationally televised games next season, tied for fourth-most in the NBA with the Boston Celtics and only behind teams like the Los Angeles Lakers, Oklahoma City Thunder, San Antonio Spurs, Philadelphia 76ers, Denver Nuggets and New York Knicks.

Being tied with one of the biggest NBA teams in the league and only trailing teams that include the defending champions and teams that feature some of the best players in the league is certainly good territory for the Timberwolves to be in, especially for a team that's in a relatively small market compared to the heavy hitters in the league.

It's a huge indication of the growth that the Timberwolves have undergone in the Edwards era and of the NBA's recognition of the star power potential of an Edwards-Ball pairing, leading the league to endure that fans are able to enjoy Minnesota basketball for over a quarter of the season.

There will certainly be big expectations for the Timberwolves this season as they have one of the best rosters they've had in years and are looking to finally get over the playoff hump and make it to the NBA Finals or even win a championship for the first time in franchise history.

It won't be an easy task, but the Timberwolves have made deep runs before and this roster, more than any other, has the chance to make history, or at least play some great basketball in the process, and no matter what happens this season, the Timberwolves will find themselves on the national stage at least 27 times.

title: Warriors’ Splash Brother gets ripped for leaving Michael Jordan out of his top-5
description: When it comes to basketball conversations about who is the greatest of all time, it's often a debate between Michael Jordan and LeBron James.
fullText:
When it comes to basketball conversations about who is the greatest of all time, it's often a debate between Michael Jordan and LeBron James. But when it comes down to top five of all time, both of them are usually a sure thing to be in it.

The X account, @MindOfBron, showed a live video of former Golden State Warriors guard Klay Thompson during a live stream with streamer PlayqueBoyMax, where Thompson revealed his shocking top-5 all-time NBA players and left Jordan off the list.

Thompson began the list by listing former Lakers great Shaquille O'Neal as his center, then put Tim Duncan and LeBron James as his two forwards.

Struggling to decide with his hand rubbing against his head, Thompson ended up choosing Kobe Bryant over Jordan at shooting guard.

"I gotta go with Kobe at the two," Thompson said. "I love Mike, but I just grew up watching Kobe. I got to play against him. 81 [point game,] twelve threes, you know, gold medals. God, I love MJ, but Kobe is like a carbon copy of Mike. Imma go, Kobe just cause that's my era."

Thompson then said he would put Steph Curry at point guard, and added that he is "loyal to my PG of the past."

Immediately after Thompson's top 5 was revealed, basketball fans across the internet commented on the post that had over 457.7 thousand views in a day and had mixed reactions about Thompson's list.

“stayed loyal to steph” no he just has common sense and knows steph is the greatest player ever at the position and it’s not relatively close

The X account @Kypsiw responded to the video and said: " 'Stayed loyal to steph' no he just has common sense and knows steph is the greatest player ever at the position and it's not relatively close."

The account @GrindHard0990 commented, "NO JORDAN FOR A REASON…DUDE A– FR…"

The backlash on Thompson continued when the account @ThehoopCentral reposted the video, and the account @ItsMichaelJ commented a GIF of Jordan hysterically laughing with a tablet in his lap.

@AriiKruse1 commented, "Great lineup, but who takes the final shot in clutch moments?"

Thompson wasn't the only one receiving backlash, as the account @Jay_Jay9517 commented on it, and took a shot at PlaqueBoyMax by saying, "These streamers are so lame, dude looks like he would rather be anywhere else than sitting next to one of the greatest NBA players of all time. .. not even engaged in the conversation."

title: Raiders Provide Key Injury Update on Banged-Up Playmaker
description: The Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver has been missing practice and didn't play in the preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals. The post Raiders Provide Key Injury Update on Banged-Up Playmaker appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Las Vegas Raiders had the worst offense in the NFL last season and one of the worst offenses in franchise history. The team addressed this by hiring Klint Kubiak as head coach, drafting Fernando Mendoza with the No. 1 pick and signing Kirk Cousins.

However, the one position group on the offense that is still unsettled is wide receiver. The Raiders were hoping that Jack Bech and Dont'e Thornton could be impact players when they drafted them last year, but neither had a strong rookie season.

Bech has been working hard to carve out a role, but there's been little talk about Thornton this training camp. A reason for that is that he's missed several practices with an undisclosed injury. This also kept him out of the first preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals.

Thornton needs to show more if he's going to have a role this season. Fortunately, it sounds like he won't be out long. Kubiak said that he's expecting Thornton to be healthy enough to see preseason action.

"He's been banged up a little bit," Kubiak told reporters.

Thornton is an athletic specimen, but he hasn't proven he can get open and catch the ball. If he does that, there aren't many cornerbacks who can cover a 6-foot-5 wide receiver who runs a 4.3 40-yard dash.

Bech immediately helped his standing in the offense with a strong game against the Cardinals. He had three catches for 25 yards and a touchdown. Plus, he made an impact as a blocker in the run game.

He's proving that he's a lot more effective in a game setting where he can be physical. Kubiak certainly took note of Bech's solid performance.

"He's a guy that has been highlighted before in our team meetings as a guy that plays really well without the football, and just so happens that when the ball finds him, he goes and makes plays," Kubiak said. "I don't think that's an accident. I think that's the kind of guy that he is, the kind of teammate that he is. Was really proud of the contested plays and critical situation plays that he made last night."

Preseason games are valuable for teams, but many teams find joint practices even more valuable. The Raiders are heading to Houston to practice with the Texans.

The Texans are one of the best teams in the NFL and arguably have the best defense. This will be an excellent test for the Raiders. Kubiak's father, Gary Kubiak, used to be the head coach of the Texans, so he's excited to work against the team he spent a lot of time around when he was younger.

"I'm really excited about next week. It's going to be extremely competitive," Kubiak said. "What a great defense that we're going to be going against, those pass rushers are impressive. Our offensive line is going to get some great work being out there in the heat. A different kind of heat will be a great challenge for us in our conditioning. This trip to Houston couldn't have come at a better time for our team."

title: Packers Discussion: How are you feeling about the team after the 1st preseason game?
description: Tell us your current thoughts on the Green Bay Packers’ roster after their preseason opener
fullText:
Since a lot of us are excited about football coming back, let's use this as a general thread to talk about the football team coming off last night's preseason opener. How are you feeling about the team? Better? Worse? Not much change? Let us know in the comments section.

Here are a couple of posts where I laid out my recent thoughts on the team:

title: Jackson Jobe ROCKED by White Sox in Return to Comerica Park
description: Jackson Jobe’s emotional return to Comerica Park took a painful turn against the first-place White Sox. Chicago tagged the young Tigers starter for nine hits and six earned runs before he escaped the fourth inning.
fullText:
Jackson Jobe's return to Comerica Park started with anticipation and ended with a hard reminder that recovery from Tommy John surgery rarely follows a straight line.

The Chicago White Sox battered Jobe for six earned runs on nine hits Friday night, knocking the Detroit Tigers right-hander out of the game after only 3⅔ innings. Jobe walked one, struck out four and left with Detroit trailing the American League Central leaders, 6-3.

It was the shortest and roughest start of Jobe's young MLB career.

Chicago refused to let Jobe settle into the comfortable rhythm he found during his season debut in San Francisco.

The White Sox scored in the opening inning and continued creating traffic against Detroit's 24-year-old starter. By the time A.J. Hinch made the walk to the mound in the fourth, Jobe had surrendered nine hits and six earned runs.

Jobe still showed flashes of the electric arsenal that has made him such an important part of Detroit's future. He struck out four and issued only one walk, suggesting his biggest problem was not wildness.

The White Sox consistently found hittable pitches in the strike zone and did not miss enough of them. Some nights, a pitcher gets beat by bloopers, defensive mistakes or bad luck. This was not one of those nights.

His season ERA climbed from 0.00 to 6.23 through his first two starts.

Friday's performance could hardly have looked more different from Jobe's first outing after completing his 14-month recovery from Tommy John surgery.

Jobe allowed one hit and one walk over five scoreless innings against the San Francisco Giants on August 8. He struck out four, earned the victory and reached 101.6 mph with his four-seam fastball.

Detroit manager A.J. Hinch called that performance "almost a perfect outing" based on what the Tigers wanted from Jobe physically and competitively.

The Tigers shut out the Giants, 8-0, and Jobe immediately looked capable of stabilizing a rotation that had been remade during the trade deadline.

Five days later, baseball delivered its correction.

The velocity and strikeout ability did not disappear. The command within the strike zone did. Chicago forced Jobe to work from the stretch, extended innings and punished pitches that caught too much of the plate.

For a pitcher still rebuilding feel after major elbow surgery, this type of outing was always possible. Detroit just hoped it would not arrive in the biggest series of the season.

Jobe's difficult night came with far more attached to it than an ordinary August start.

The Tigers began Friday 2½ games behind the first-place White Sox in the AL Central. A three-game sweep at Comerica Park would have moved Detroit into first place.

Instead of giving the Tigers an early advantage, Jobe put them in comeback mode.

Detroit entered the series playing its best baseball of the season, winning nine of 12 games and taking two of three from the Cleveland Guardians. The Tigers closed that series with one of the strangest pitching performances in franchise history, a 3-0 shutout completed without recording a strikeout.

The next night brought the opposite problem. Detroit's starter missed enough bats to record four strikeouts, but he could not keep Chicago from piling up hits.

That is baseball's sense of humor.

The Tigers need Jobe to help their postseason push, but they cannot allow one ugly performance to change the long-term plan.

Jobe underwent a hybrid Tommy John procedure in June 2025. His return followed more than a year of rehabilitation, bullpen sessions, simulated games and minor-league starts. He discussed the emotional side of that journey before returning to Detroit, calling the experience a "blessing in disguise" and explaining how the time away helped him develop beyond baseball.

That full story is available in Detroit Sports Nation's feature on Jobe's emotional road back to the Tigers.

Detroit has every reason to remain careful. The organization cannot chase a division title by treating Jobe like a veteran prepared to throw 100 pitches every fifth day.

Friday's 3⅔-inning outing will create additional bullpen stress during a crucial series. It should not tempt the Tigers to accelerate Jobe's workload during his next start.

His health still matters more than the standings.

Jobe's performance deserves criticism. Six earned runs and nine hits in fewer than four innings is a poor outing under any circumstances.

The former No. 3 overall pick remains only two appearances into his return from reconstructive elbow surgery. He showed elite velocity in San Francisco and retained enough swing-and-miss ability to strike out four White Sox on Friday.

Can Jobe locate his fastball more effectively? Can he use his secondary pitches to avoid predictable counts? Can he slow an inning before three singles become a crooked number?

Those questions matter more than the inflated ERA attached to a tiny sample.

Detroit did not bring Jobe back because it expected perfection. The Tigers brought him back because they believe his talent can help them now and anchor their rotation for years.

Friday night was the ugly side of that process.

Jackson Jobe was rocked in his return to Comerica Park, allowing six earned runs and nine hits over 3⅔ innings against the first-place Chicago White Sox.

The timing made the performance sting even more. Detroit entered the series with a chance to take control of the AL Central race, only to watch its prized young starter put the Tigers in an early hole.

Jobe's first start showed why Detroit believes in him. His second showed how much work remains after Tommy John surgery.

One rough night does not change his future. It does make the Tigers' path through this critical series considerably more difficult.

title: How Scottie Scheffler delivered just what Memphis golf fans needed at the St. Jude
description: Scottie Scheffler dialed up a well-timed dandy at TPC Southwind — and for that, we thank him.
fullText:
MEMPHIS, TN — Scottie Scheffler dialed up a well-timed dandy at TPC Southwind on Friday, Aug. 14 — and for that, we thank him.

With the unrelenting, unforgiving Memphis-in-August heat index stretching north of 110 degrees and squeezing some of the life out of the FedEx St. Jude Championship — itself already besieged by a strong undercurrent of angst and awkwardness — the best golfer in the world tied the course record with a second-round 61, giving us all something we sorely needed.

A reason to focus on actual golf.

Scheffler's sensational scorcher, tied for the third-lowest round of his career, provided everyone with a distraction from the shoddy hand the PGA Tour dealt the longstanding annual tournament just a week before it started. A diversion from the uncertain future, lingering overhead like a sword of Damocles. A respite for fans braving the sweltering conditions.

Perhaps even the tour appreciates another brilliant round from Scheffler — if for no other reason than maybe to stem the tide of bitterness being directed its way in the wake of its recent decision to strip the Memphis event of its lofty status starting in 2028.

Needing a birdie on No. 18 to establish a new low round at the 37-year-old course, Scheffler casually waved to his wife, Meredith, and their eldest son, Bennett, who were looking on from the back porch of a house located just behind the 18th tee box.

Scheffler admitted (in a post-round interview with The Golf Channel) that his focus shifted in that moment to an issue a bit more unnerving than the humid press of the scalding afternoon sun or the pressure of precision with history on the line.

"Yeah, I was a little worried," he began. "When the (pacifier is) in midday, that means he's not feeling so good. The passy made me a little nervous, so I'll get home and check on him pretty quick."

A few minutes later, his 15-foot, 7-inch birdie putt came up a mere 8 inches short.

More: FedEx Cup Playoffs bubble: Who's up, who's down in top 50 after Round 2 at St. Jude

But it couldn't spoil another outstanding outing for Scheffler, who became the fifth professional to card a 61 at TPC Southwind — where he made his debut as a professional golfer in 2018 at the St. Jude Classic. In the same city where Al Geiberger was christened "Mr. 59," becoming the first golfer on the PGA Tour to shoot a 59 (at Colonial Country Club in 1977, when the event was known as the Danny Thomas Memphis Classic), Scheffler joined Justin Rose (2023), Tom Lewis (2020), Bob Estes (2001) and Jay Delsing (1993) at the top of TPC Southwind lore.

When does it register for Scheffler that he's having an incredible day?

"Probably not till the round's over," he said.

His personal-best in tournament play is a 59, which he achieved at The Northern Trust in 2020 — the first leg of the FedEx Cup Playoffs that year. The FedEx St. Jude Championship has been the opening event of the postseason since 2022, and will stay that way until after the 2027 tournament.

Whether professional golf continues in Memphis for a 70th consecutive year remains uncertain. Even if it does, the prestige attached to it since 2019 (when it was elevated to a signature event) will be greatly diminished.

In a way, Scheffler's showing serves as only another reminder of the kind of world-class level of excellence Memphis is losing. Something even Scheffler can't help but rue.

"We love coming back to Memphis," he said before the tournament began. "Hopefully, it will be part of it in some capacity.

"Yeah, if it's not, I'll definitely be sad to see it leave."

But at least for part of Friday, the conversation drifted from the worry of what's to come, because Scheffler gave us all something else to think about. Something to appreciate.

"It's so cliche to say you can't do anything about it, isn't it?" said Tommy Fleetwood, the 2025 FedEx Cup Playoffs champ. "It's sort of a boring answer, but what can we do about Scottie Scheffler?"

title: Who’s to Blame for the Houston Rockets Missing 27 Straight Threes?
description: A historic shooting collapse cost Houston a trip to the Finals, but scapegoating James Harden ignores a team-wide meltdown based on a team-wide philosophy. There's plenty of blame to go around in this historic collapse.
fullText:
Back in the 2018 NBA Playoffs, the Houston Rockets became the laughing stock of the NBA world. Maybe even the whole basketball world, or the world of sports in general. This, of course, is when they blew their chance at an NBA Finals appearance by missing 27 consecutive threes in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals.

The crazy thing is that it was still a single digit loss with the scoreboard reading 101-92 at the end, per the ESPN Box Score. That means the Rockets could've forced overtime if they made three more shots from distance. Instead, they shot 10/44 overall, only making one of their last thirty attempts. It was just the ultimate cold streak at the worst possible time.

I often see fans, media members, and even former players blaming James Harden, which I'll never fully understand. They act as if he missed all 27 of those three pointers by himself. He did miss 10 straight, which is more than a third of that infamous slump, but that leaves 17 more attempts without a make.

Harden shot 2/13 from deep, but Eric Gordon wasn't much better. He finished shooting only 2/12, missing seven consecutive threes to add to The Beard's 10 straight. Trevor Ariza went 0/9 on the night, with six of those coming in the team's cold spell.

So just three guys were responsible for 23 straight misses, and combined to shoot 4/34 overall. It was a team-wide meltdown, not just Harden. That's because launching threes was a team-wide mandate for everyone, not just Harden. Clint Capela was the only guy prohibited from taking any.

PJ Tucker was the best shooter in black and red that night, though, making two out of his five attempts. Gerald Green only shot one for four. Ryan Anderson didn't miss, but that's only because he didn't take any shots in his eight minutes of play. Even Joe Johnson missed his only attempt in his five minutes on the court. It was the whole team.

Since 2012-2013, the Rockets were at the top of the league for three pointers attempted per game in every season besides 2015-2016, per Team-Rankings. They still only attempted 1.1 less than the Warriors in their 73-9 season, where Stephen Curry made an NBA record 402 threes by himself.

Point being, this is what the Rockets did and they found great success with it. 2018 was no different, as James Harden was finally awarded MVP in that season. In the previous year, Mike D'Antoni won Coach of the year and Eric Gordon won Sixth Man of the Year. They were at the peak of their powers.

It's hard to expect any player, let alone a whole team, to completely switch their successful style of play after missing some shots. They played their game and they lost, so who's to blame?

Coaching, for not switching up the strategy and still relying on the law of averages in the biggest game of the season? All of the players, for following that game plan?

Or just specifically James Harden? Blame him for continuing to play the team's style of ball, rather than going rogue and doing his own thing? Going against his teammates and coaches by randomly taking some mid range jumpers?

I just can't personally get with that idea. They took a page out of the Philadelphia 76ers book and trusted the process. The playstyle was always going to be limiting, but they trusted the mathematics behind it. Three is greater than two. They just didn't make enough threes.

If they don't live by the three for the greater part of the 2010's, then sure, they don't die by the three in the 2018 WCF either —— but that also means you don't get any of the 50 win seasons with multiple All-Stars, or the franchise record 65 win season in 2018.

It was a bitter ending, but sometimes that's just the way it goes. No need to place blame on anyone for the shortcomings, in my opinion. All that does is take away from the greatness that we saw in that Harden era of Houston Rockets basketball.

title: The Astros Were 11 Games Under .500 in May. Now They're Running the AL West
description: The Houston Astros went from being one of the worst teams in the league to leading the AL West. They were below .500 for most of the season, and now they're trying to hold onto the division lead.
fullText:
At the start of the season, the Astros struggled with injury after injury, and the pitching staff especially took a hit. Spencer Arrighetti, who was recently traded to the Blue Jays for Daulton Varsho, was named the AL's Pitcher of the Month in May, but he wasn't the same when June rolled around.

They also lost Carlos Correa early on, and until a few weeks ago, it looked like he might be out for the entire season. Peña missed real time too, over a month with a hamstring strain in the spring, then another IL stint in late June with a calf strain. With only a few players left, the Astros were barely holding on, but now that almost everyone is back, they are a completely different team.

After falling to a season-low 11 games under .500 following a May 14 loss to Seattle, Houston started making their way back. They won 2 of 3 against Texas right after, then took 7 of 10 on a road trip. It was a slow, grinding climb back toward .500 through May and June, no big streak, just steady progress. Two steps forward, one step back kind of season.

Then came a real setback. Houston got swept by the Orioles right after the All-Star break, falling back to 7 games under .500 and undoing a lot of progress. From there, it looked like they weren't going to get back on the upswing.

But they answered immediately, with an 11-1 run, their best stretch in a full calendar year. That run changed everything and sent them past both Seattle and Texas and into first place in the AL West.

Now that the injury list is shrinking, the Astros seem to have found their rhythm, and they found it when it mattered most. They fell off a little in their series against the Padres, but bounced back with a series win against the Giants during their West Coast trip. Now they head into this series against the Mariners with momentum and a solid pitching plan.

The Astros are heading home from a series win and into a special moment this weekend. Daikin Park is also honoring Alan Ashby and the late Phil Garner into the Astros Hall of Fame this weekend, adding some occasion to the series.

Aside from this season being a pretty impressive comeback, it would be a shame to have a player like Yordan Alvarez miss out on the playoffs two seasons in a row after the season he's had. Through all of the rough patches, Alvarez has been crushing at the plate all season.

Houston sits at 62-60 today, in first place, and this weekend against a fading Mariners team is the next real test of whether this turnaround is going to propel them into the playoffs.

title: Commanders' Dorance Armstrong suspended for season opener vs. Eagles

fullText:
Washington Commanders defensive end Dorance Armstrong has been suspended for the first game of the season for violating the NFL's Personal Conduct Policy. He will be eligible to participate in all preseason activities, including playing in Washington's preseason games.

When Armstrong returns against the Cowboys in Week 2, it will be his first game since tearing his ACL against Dallas in Week 7 of last season. Prior to his torn ACL, Armstrong was having arguably the best season of his career with 5.5 sacks and seven tackles for loss in just seven games.

This year will be his third year with the Commanders and ninth season in the NFL. Armstrong spent the first six seasons of his career with Dallas, where he recorded a total of 23.5 sacks, 169 total tackles, and 48 quarterback hits. He has been a starter for most of his time with Washington and is expected to play a big role in the Commanders' defensive rotation this season.

title: Who is, isn’t playing for Seahawks exhibition vs Dallas; Lawrence’s final year
description: Coach Mike Macdonald, new offensive coordinator Brian Fleury to change how Seattle uses quarterbacks Drew Lock, Jalen Milroe in these games.
fullText:
If you want to see most of the Seahawks regulars who won the Super Bowl six months ago playing again, you may have to wait until the opener next month.

Or buy a ticket to Nashville for next week.

The Seahawks are back inside Lumen Field Saturday evening to play a game for the first time since they won the NFC championship there over the Los Angeles Rams in late January. Twenty of the 22 starters for Seattle in that home title game 6 1/2 months ago are back for this season.

But almost all the guys who won that game and got Seattle into Super Bowl 60 will be watching, not playing, Saturday during the first preseason game for the new season, against the Dallas Cowboys (5 p.m., KING-5 television).

"A lot of our established starters won't be playing. They'll be going through the warmup and everything," coach Mike Macdonald said following his Seahawks' light, walk-through practice Friday.

Quarterback Sam Darnold will not play, Macdonald said.

Others almost assuredly not playing: 2025 NFL offensive player of the year Jaxon Smith-Njigba, 2021 offensive player of the year and Super Bowl MVP Cooper Kupp, three-time Pro Bowl cornerback Devon Witherspoon, Pro Bowl veteran defensive lineman Leonard Williams and outside linebacker DeMarcus Lawrence, middle linebacker Ernest Jones and emerging tight end AJ Barner.

Lawrence, 34, in his 13th NFL training camp, told Yahoo! Sports' Jori Epstein Thursday this will be his final season. Lawrence's wife Sasha and their six children are living in the Dallas area while the Cowboy for the first 11 years of his pro career plays a second season in Seattle.

He considered retiring this past offseason.

"It was a tough process," Lawrence told Epstein, a former Cowboys beat writer. "But through the grace of God, I'm able to play another year and soak it all up one more good time before I hang it up."

If Macdonald does as he did in his first two summers as Seattle's coach, in August of 2024 and '25, the starters' only time playing against another team in the preseason will be in the Seahawks' joint practice.

#Seahawks QB Sam Darnold on borrow a Green Bay kid’s bike to ride to joint practice vs Packers: “Incredible.

“Didn’t get a chance to raise the seat though.”

Said it was really cool to talk to the bike owner who was carrying his helmet walking beside him. “Incredible tradition.” pic.twitter.com/6shOX5HjKZ

The Seahawks and Titans play their second preseason game Sunday, Aug. 23 in Nashville.

Veteran backup Drew Lock will start at quarterback Saturday. Jalen Milroe, Seattle's third-round draft choice last year, will enter the game — but not necessarily finish it. New offensive coordinator Brian Fleury plans on rotating Lock and Milroe in and out of the former San Francisco 49ers tight end coach's first game as an offensive play-caller at any level.

That's a departure from how Macdonald's first two Seahawks teams did the quarterbacks in the preseason. Lock started, and the third-stringer entered then finished the game. Or Milroe played the entire game, as he did last August at Green Bay in the preseason finale of his rookie year.

"The quarterbacks, we're going to rotate in some form or fashion. We have an idea of how we want it to work, but don't want to be put in a corner there," Macdonald said. "It'll be great. Both guys will get great experience with playing with different units and it'll be good."

"Normally a quarterback goes until he doesn't go and then the next guy goes and closes the game out. This game, I think we're going to rotate them to some extent."

Milroe is looking forward to showing off his progress from last year as a complete passer. That's what Fleury and his coaches are focusing on with him.

They know Milroe can run, as he did for three plays in three games early last season in a special package from then-OC Klint Kubiak.

Accuracy throwing the ball on time, with anticipation, that's what coaches are seeking from Milroe in the preseason games this month.

Milroe began this training camp inaccurate throwing. Then in the first week of August he had some of his best practices since the Seahawks drafted him in the spring of 2025. This week, he's been off at times again in his accuracy throwing to his receivers.

He says he needs to let it rip Saturday against Dallas.

"Being decisive, I think that's so important," Milroe said. "You see it with the quarterback's feet, and they're playing on time and they're letting the ball go.

"It's all about being decisive."

That's how Monty Python's "Meaning of Life" would describe the Seahawks' situation at the position Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker left to sign with Kansas City this spring.

Top rookie Jadarian Price will not play Saturday. The first-round draft choice and presumed lead back to replace Walker has missed the last five full practices because of "upper-leg soreness," as Macdonald has termed it.

Price was in the starting offense walking through plays in the light practice Friday. He did the same thing in an "ACT" (alignment, communication, technique) practice Wednesday.

"He is on the mend," the head coach said of Price.

Zach Charbonnet remains on the physically-unable-to-perform list. He had reconstructive knee surgery in February. He may not be ready to play until after the season begins Sept. 9 against New England.

Emmanuel Wilson was getting time with the starting offense through last weekend. Then he pulled up running out of bounds and grabbed his hamstring late in a scrimmage that ended practice Tuesday.

"It's a short-term thing," Macdonald said.

Jacardia Wright has missed the last week of practices after he injured his lower leg during a scrimmage in early August.

That leaves George Holani as the only back with any experience playing for the Seahawks to play the preseason game Saturday.

"George should see some action to some degree," Macdonald said.

Expect a lot of carries and time for undrafted rookies Justin Jones and T.J. Harden, plus for 2025 practice-squad player Velus Jones Jr.

Justin Jones, mostly a special-teams player at Auburn, signed six days ago.

To get an idea of how thin Harden got a pitch from Darnold on the first-team offense in the red zone on the final play of practice Thursday. Harden, from SMU, signed nine days ago.

Last preseason, Macdonald's favorite plays were the penalties his Seahawks starters and veterans got for coming off the sideline and celebrating big plays by the younger reserves.

He calls that the "cost of doing business" the way he wants his Seahawks to play, with supreme emotion and togetherness.

"I'm excited to see our guys play tomorrow. They have been working incredibly hard," Macdonald said. "You talk about layering training camp. We start with the ramp process, you go into the stadium practice, get ones on ones, all these different types of periods. Now we're layering it again with another team in our stadium, so there's more conditions that you add to the whole training process.

"I'm eager for our team to be us in those situations. Our players have earned the right, in my opinion, throughout this process, to go let it rip and trust your training and go have fun. Go play football that they know how and our brand of ball.

"Hopefully it comes to life — and hopefully we have some cost-of-doing-business celebration penalties."

title: What Happened to Marcus Mariota? Latest Update on Commanders QB After Scary Non-Contact Injury in Preseason

title: AD Alford: ‘Excitement Around Seminoles Football is High’
description: Florida State athletic director Michael Alford was interviewed on the ACC Huddle: Florida State Road Trip. He offered some insights into how Florida State is competing with its peers in the arena of college athletics.
fullText:
For thelast seven years, Florida State athletic director Michael Alford has crisscrossedthe southeastern portion of the United States championing his university toboosters, parents and potential student athletes.

His mission: raise funds andrecruit talent to Florida State.

On the ACCHuddle-Florida State Road Trip show, Alford was interviewed, and he offeredsome insights into the "business" end of college football.

"When I arrivedsix, seven years ago, Florida State was not up to par to what our peers were,and we had to invest in the resources," said Alford. "Offering a holistic view,we have a top 25 public education we can offer, now we got these facilities.And, when you come and train mind, body and soul, then you have to invest in thetalent acquisition. We are doing that at a high level and giving them the bestof both worlds in coming to Florida State. It really represents what FloridaState is about, the class of this university, the community and our program."

So far,this year has been the most successful year of fundraising for Florida Stateboosters, bringing in a record-setting $106 million. Alford and his departmentare committed to providing all that is necessary to help his teams be competitive,and ultimately win.

"You haveto invest and give them the resources," said Alford. "In the last severalyears, we've done over $550 million in renovations. We are giving them theresources, now they got to go produce."

Unfortunately,that production has not materialized on the gridiron for the Seminoles. 17losses in their last 24 games is not a good return on investment, by anymeasure. But as the new season approaches, Alford said. "Excitement around thisteam is high."

Astraining camp draws to a close and the week zero game with New Mexico State is uponus, fans and the media could see coach Mike Norvell lead a different FloridaState team out of the tunnel at Doak Campbell Stadium.

Men with adesire to be better versions of themselves, to play together as a band ofbrothers, forged in blood, sweat and tears. They endured the blistering summerheat to transform themselves into warriors in search of gridiron glory, notonly for themselves, but for a grateful fan base.

Players flirtedwith the transfer portal, but changed their minds and returned because they believedin their development within the Seminoles program. Coaches stayed, trained theirplayers hard over the summer leading up to fall camp. Camp is where boys becomemen, hardened by the daily grind, chipping away at the player he was and becominga player with a different mindset.

Lastseason, four of Florida State's losses were by eight points or fewer. Apositive play here or there would have meant the difference between a 5-7 losingseason, and a respectable 9-3 season.

title: Mike Macdonald addresses Seahawks’ controversial Terrion Arnold signing
description: Macdonald said the Seahawks did their due diligence on the troubled former first round pick.
fullText:
Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald spoke about the team's controversial decision to sign former Detroit Lions first-round pick Terrion Arnold, who is facing several felony charges in Florida.

Following Friday's practice for their preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys, Macdonald was asked several questions about the decision, from how they view him as a player to his fit in the culture. Macdonald declined to comment on anything regarding Arnold's current legal proceedings, saying the team would allow the league and court processes to play out.

"I think it was an opportunity to bring on a player that we felt strongly about during the draft process," Macdonald told the media. 'We also understand that it's a serious situation with a legal matter. There's a process behind it, so we respect that. That's how we'll operate too, just letting that process play out and let the league decide if and when his return to play is."

Seattle hosted the former Alabama star for a tryout on Sunday, which Macdonald described as "great." Macdonald said that he spoke to several people, whom he respects, about Arnold, and they supported him as a person. He added that he had informal one-on-one conversations with players prior to signing the former first-round pick and that he was confident in the team's locker room and team.

"I referenced the folks that had been in his corner throughout the process as well and we respect those people. We're not going to ignore those folks that we really respect, and have a strong opinion about it as well," Macdonald said. "When you put all of those things together, it felt like it was a good opportunity for the team."

While the team has agreed to terms with Arnold, Macdonald said the Seahawks are still working through a timeline for him to join the team, meaning he won't be suiting up for the Seahawks in their preseason opener on Saturday night. Additionally, the NFL has the option to place Arnold on the Commissioner's Exempt List, which would bar him from playing any regular season games.

"All I know is that there's an availability, if the league lets it happen, that he could play. In terms of when that happens and how that goes down, it's just part of that process," Macdonald said. "The facts of the case, all those things about the comments of what happens, that's not our responsibility to have a comment on that nor can we. I think we just have to understand that there's a process at play, and we're going to let it play out."

When asked about Arnold as a player, Macdonald lauded Arnold's physicality and speed, saying that his skill set fits the identity of the secondary. The Seahawks head coach said Arnold is used to some of the pattern matching that the Seahawks do from his time at Alabama and that he believes there's a spot for him if he becomes the best version of himself.

"We want players to come in and be the best version of themselves," Macdonald said. "We believe that if you do that, then the team's going to be better for it as well. Terrion [Arnold] will be the same process with him if or when he gets here."

The signing is meant to bolster a Seahawks cornerback group that lost Riq Woolen this offseason and is set to rely on inexperienced players, like Nehemiah Pritchett and rookies Julian Neal and Michael Dansby, to fill the role.

title: Buffalo Bills Have Checked In on Trade for Star Defensive Tackle
description: The Buffalo Bills have checked on the availability of a star defensive tackle.
fullText:
The Buffalo Bills are among the teams that have checked on the availability of star defensive tackle Vita Vea. Vea requested a trade earlier this offseason, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers do not want to trade him.

Vea is one of the best interior defensive linemen in the league and is coming off another productive season. In 2025, Vea finished with 34 total tackles, seven tackles for loss, 4.5 sacks, two pass deflections, and a fumble recovery.

The 31-year-old is an elite run-stuffer and quality pass rusher, entering the final year of his contract, worth $17 million.

If the Buccaneers change their tune and decide to trade Vea, he could be a great piece for the Bills' defensive line alongside Ed Oliver on the interior with edge rushers Bradley Chubb, TJ Parker, and Greg Rousseau.

Oliver was off to a dominant start in the 2025 season, as he had 12 total tackles, seven tackles for loss, three sacks, and a forced fumble through three games. If he stays healthy, he could be one of the best defensive tackles in the league in 2026.

Off the edge, Buffalo added Chubb in free agency on a three-year $43.5 million deal while drafting Parker in the second round.

Chubb played at a high level for the Miami Dolphins in 2025, recording 47 total tackles, eight tackles for loss, 8.5 sacks, two forced fumbles, and a fumble recovery. He will be an impactful pass rusher off the edge for the Bills.

Buffalo will also hope that Parker can translate his college success to the NFL. Parker had 126 total tackles, 41.5 tackles for loss, 21.5 sacks, six forced fumbles, and six fumble recoveries across three seasons at Clemson.

Rousseau is the other established piece off the edge for the Bills, as he had 46 total tackles, six tackles for loss, seven sacks, and a forced fumble in the 2025 season.

Buffalo is looking to make a Super Bowl push in the 2026 season with Josh Allen as their superstar quarterback. If the Bills acquire Vea for their defense, it will help them in their pursuit of a Lombardi Trophy.

title: Boxing star Claressa Shields has it all. Well, expect for knockouts. Does that matter?
description: Claressa Shields has won two Olympic gold medals, 19 world titles and is 18-0 as a pro, but she has only three knockouts. Does that matter?
fullText:
As a star boxer, Claressa Shields has it all. Well, almost.

Two Olympic gold medals. Nineteen world titles. A pro record of 18-0.

"I have more knockouts than she has wins,'' Laila Ali said last yaer.

Indeed, Ali does, having finished her career 24-0 with 21 knockouts.

Shields will have another chance to quiet critics when she fights Kaye Scott for the WBA and WBC women's middleweight world titles Saturday, Aug. 15 at State Farm Arena in Atlanta.

"I care a little bit,'' Shields said during preparations for the fight. "Who doesn't want a knockout?  But at the end of the day, a win is a win.''

But when it comes to legacy, is a win a win? Will a lack of knockouts tarnish Shields' legacy?

"Absolutely not,'' Malissa Smith, a women's boxing historian, told USA TODAY Sports. "Claressa Shields is a once in a generation kind of fighter.''

Shields, 31, enters the fight against Scott as a massive -3000 favorite, which converts to a 97% probability of her winning the fight. She is +150 to win by KO, TKO or DQ, which converts to a 40% probability that the fight will end by stoppage.

That signals a sense of optimism, considering Shields has won only 16.7% of her fights by knockout.

The topic of knockouts can ruffle Shields.

"I don't know why you all think you be offending somebody by telling me, 'oh, you got three knockouts,'" she said this month. "I got 19 world titles on top of five different divisions. And I make the most money with the least knockouts. ... It don't matter.''

In February, Shields addressed the subject before her fight against Franchon Crews Dezurn.

"If you look at my record, the only thing I don't have is knockouts,'' she said. "I have the championships. I have the undisputed titles. I have all the divisions.

"Now it's like, dang, how about we get some more knockouts? So I've been pushing myself for that.''

On Aug. 21, Amanda Serrano will have a chance to set a new record for knockouts by a female boxer when she fights Lucrecia Manzur in a featherweight title bout. She and retired boxer Christy Martin are tied with 32 knockouts.

Shields posted photos of her and Serrano side-by-side with this caption: "The most knockouts don't mean you're the most skilled.'' With a typo but conviction, she also wrote, "GOWAT REIGNS SUPREME.''

Smith, author of ''The Promise of Women's Boxing,'' concurs.

"I'm not taking anything away from Amanda Serrano, believe me. But a lot of her knockouts are TKOs that occurred earlier in her career,'' Smith said.

Serrano is coming off a TKO over Cheyenne Hanson in May. But Smith also pointed out that before Serrano stopped Stevie Morgan by TKO in 2024, she had not knocked out an opponent since 2021.

In Serrano's last 12 fights, she has two knockouts.

But even if she gets the record, she won't be defined by KOs as much as having won nine major titles in seven divisions.

Martin possessed great power and a ferocity inside the ring. But she is known just as much for being a trailblazer, the first female boxer to fight on a pay-per-view card and the first to appear on the cover of Sports Illustrated.

Neither can match the accolades Shields has collected as an amateur and a pro.

During a recent appearance on Max Kellerman's boxing show, Shields claimed she could beat Rolly Romero, the men's WBA welterweight champion.

"What size gloves?'' Kellerman asked.

"What size gloves?'' Shields shot back. "Do you not see this face? I don't even get hit.''

Although Shields has never been a knockout artist, her boxing artistry derives from a combination of defense, footwork, quickness and punching volume.

With Serrano likely to break the knockout record, Smith said she expects Serrano to be a first-ballot inductee into the International Boxing Hall of Fame.

"But Shields is something else,'' Smith said. "With Shields, it's like, 'Oh, you're big. You should be getting KOs.' (But) she puts on incredibly exciting bouts and everybody watching her goes, 'Oh my God.' "

"It might be just a matter of physics, how you're executing the torque, how you're finding that mark,'' Smith said. "It's not for lack of trying. I mean, she hits hard. That's for sure.''

Shields recorded her first knockout as a pro in her second fight, when she stopped Szilvia Szabados by TKO in the fourth round of their middleweight bout in March 2017.

Shields got her second knockout in the fourth fight of her pro career. She stopped Nikki Adler in the fifth round of their super middleweight title fight in August 2017.

Shields got her third in July 2024, when she stopped Vanessa Lepage-Joanisse by TKO in the second round of their heavyweight title fight. Shields knocked down Lepage-Joanisse three times in the second round before the referee halted the fight.

Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa made his preseason debut with the Falcons on Friday night against the Broncos.

In two drives led by Tua, the Falcons punted twice.

title: Good Sports: Fresno dad turns hobby into unforgettable moment with Dallas Cowboys QB Dak Prescott
description: A Fresno father's custom tribute hat for Dak Prescott turned a year-old painting hobby into an unforgettable, full-circle moment.
fullText:
A Fresno father's painting hobby led to an unforgettable encounter when Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott not only accepted one of his custom hats, but later wore it and sought out the artist behind it.

Mario Corona, a stay-at-home dad, licensed EMT and aspiring firefighter, began painting hats about a year ago. He said he never expected one of his designs would end up in the hands of an NFL quarterback.

"A day that I definitely won't forget," Corona said.

Recently, Corona completed a Dallas Cowboys collection that included a tribute to Prescott's brother, Jace. Prescott lost his brother to suicide in 2020 and has spoken publicly about raising awareness since then.

Corona created what he calls an "Angel Hat," featuring a portrait of Jace on the side.

"I know as a Cowboys fan, as a Dak fan, I know how much his brother meant to him and his motivation," Corona said.

Corona traveled to Cowboys training camp in Oxnard hoping to personally give the hat to Prescott. During First Responders Appreciation Day, he was able to get on the field.

"The players right in front of Dak were CeeDee [Lamb] and [George] Pickens, which were the players that were on my hat that I was wearing at the time. So I got caught up in trying to show them the hat I was wearing," Corona said. "By the time they passed and I turned back, Dak was already right here. I just babbled out whatever words were trying to come out of my mouth. Luckily, he did grab it before walking off."

Prescott accepted the hat without initially noticing the portrait painted on its side.

"I was happy that I knew he took it at least. I was actually leaving training camp pretty bummed. I didn't sell any hats, I didn't get any autographs," Corona said.

After leaving camp, Corona saw photos on social media showing Prescott wearing the hat. That is when he learned the quarterback was looking for the artist who created it.

"Got in the car, drove back... they're like, dude, you're going to have to go to the hotel," Corona said.

Corona later reunited with Prescott and captured the interaction on his Meta glasses.

"It was just real. It felt real," Corona said. "You know that moment was bigger than an autograph."

Throughout the remainder of training camp, Prescott was seen wearing Corona's hat.

The positive response to his work has encouraged Corona to take the next step with his business. He said he plans to open for commissions in November.

"As long as you're passionate about it and you stay dedicated... progress will come. If you're trying, you're going to have improvement. It for sure has paid off," Corona said.

Griner ultimately played, but she logged only 19 minutes and finished with five points, seven rebounds and four assists in a 104-69 loss.

Her remaining on the injury report suggests Connecticut is not yet comfortable declaring the knee issue resolved. Griner has played in only 18 of the Sun's first 32 games this season. Despite the interruptions, she is averaging 13.2 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.8 blocks while shooting 52.7% from the field.

Those numbers prove she can still control stretches of games. The larger question is how often her body will allow her to do it.

Griner is not Connecticut's only frontcourt concern. Edwards also could miss Saturday's game because of a left ankle injury. Her presence would become even more important if Griner cannot play.

The Sun already face a significant size and rebounding challenge against New York. Jones remains one of the league's most imposing interior players, while Stewart can score from nearly anywhere on the floor. Connecticut needs Griner's rim protection to discourage drives and contest Jones around the basket. It needs Edwards' mobility and physicality to defend Stewart, rebound and create second opportunities.

Without both, the Sun could be forced to rely heavily on Olivia Nelson-Ododa and Raegan Beers while using smaller lineups for extended stretches.

That approach could improve Connecticut's pace, but it also would leave the team vulnerable on the glass and inside the paint. The Liberty have recently overwhelmed opponents with their rebounding. Giving Jones and Stewart repeated second-chance opportunities would be a recipe for another long afternoon.

Thursday's loss demonstrated how quickly games can get away from the Sun. Atlanta scored 104 points and won by 35. Angel Reese controlled the interior with 15 rebounds, while the Dream repeatedly turned Connecticut's defensive breakdowns into easy scoring opportunities.

Now the Sun must prepare for an opponent with even more proven offensive weapons. New York owns a 21-14 record and recently defeated the Los Angeles Sparks 85-81. The Liberty nearly squandered a 28-point fourth-quarter lead, but Sabrina Ionescu made critical free throws to secure the victory.

The Liberty are dealing with injury concerns of their own. Satou Sabally is out while recovering from lingering concussion symptoms, Leonie Fiebich is sidelined by a foot injury and Ionescu is listed as questionable with a foot issue. That creates at least some hope for Connecticut.

New York, however, still can turn to Stewart, Jones, Marine Johannès and a deep collection of experienced contributors. Johannès recently scored a career-high 27 points while hitting seven 3-pointers in a 111-71 victory over the Las Vegas Aces. Connecticut cannot spend the opening quarter attempting to find its energy. The Sun must defend with urgency, limit turnovers and establish some offensive rhythm before New York begins dictating the game.

Griner's final designation will affect almost every part of the Sun's game plan. If she plays, Connecticut can work through her in the post and force Jones to defend rather than allowing her to roam near the rim. Griner also gives the Sun a reliable target when their perimeter offense stalls.

Her defensive impact might be even more important. Griner's size allows Connecticut's guards to apply more pressure knowing an elite shot-blocker is stationed behind them.

If she sits, the Sun will have to play faster and generate more offense from their guards and wings. Saniya Rivers and Leila Lacan could receive increased responsibility, while Connecticut may rely more heavily on transition opportunities.

Neither option guarantees success against the Liberty.

That is what makes Griner's latest injury update so concerning. The Sun are not merely waiting to see whether one player will be available. They are waiting to learn which version of their team can take the floor.

Connecticut's 8-24 record makes a late playoff push increasingly unlikely. That reality should influence how the organization handles Griner.

The Sun would benefit from having their veteran center against New York, but risking further damage to her knee for one regular-season game would make little sense. Griner already has missed 14 games and recently returned from a four-game absence caused by the same injury.

Connecticut must determine whether she is truly ready for another physical matchup. If Griner plays, her minutes could remain limited. If she sits, the Sun will have to find another way to survive against one of the WNBA's strongest frontcourts.

Either way, Saturday's final injury report could shape the entire game before the ball is tipped.

title: Tagovailoa, Falcons offense struggle to get started in his brief Atlanta debut
description: Tua Tagovailoa faced heavy pressure in his two series of work Friday night against the Denver Broncos.
fullText:
Tua Tagovailoa's Falcons preseason debut Friday showed that he and the rest of Atlanta's offense have some work to do.

Granted, it was a brief outing, with Tagovailoa playing only two series with the starters in Atlanta against the Denver Broncos, and it wasn't the full lineup. Running back Bijan Robinson and right tackle Jawaan Taylor both sat out, and Drake London played only a few snaps.

But even against a good Denver defense that fielded some of its starting unit, the Falcons showed little of the firepower they're hoping for in the regular season, with their three main playmakers back.

On Tagovailoa's first series, the Falcons went three-and-out. He dropped a shotgun snap that hit him squarely in the hands, leading to a sack, and Atlanta punted one play later.

Tua fumbles the snap pic.twitter.com/hP5rsAzKom

The second series wasn't much better. The Broncos were getting pressure often, with Tagovailoa having to throw multiple passes away. He was hit hard on third down, which might have led head coach Kevin Stefanski to say no mas.

Tagovailoa finished his outing 3-for-5 passing for 22 yards. He targeted tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. on four of his five passes, often under duress.

With Michael Penix Jr. still out with injury, Cooper Rush replaced Tagovailoa and promptly was picked on his second pass attempt of the game.

It's hard to judge the Falcons' offensive performance in a vacuum Friday. The biggest eyesore was the pressure the offensive line surrendered, with Michael Jerrell replacing Taylor. The blocking wasn't great.

They'll want to get that ironed out before the next preseason game, and certainly prior to Week 1 against the Steelers. Tagovailoa needs all the clean pockets he can get if he wants to fend off Penix this whole season.

title: Mets' Juan Soto expects to return before end of season: 'Why not try to rejoin this team?'
description: Mets outfielder Juan Soto expressed his desire to return to the team before the end of the 2026 season as he continues his recovery from a left calf strain.
fullText:
Juan Soto, the Mets' biggest bat and their biggest star, has been out with a calf injury since late July, but wants to return to the team before the end of the 2026 season.

With New York's playoff chances dwindling after being sellers at the trade deadline, it would be understandable if Soto was shut down for the rest of the year as he recovers, but the Mets' lone All-Star this season vows to be back with this team.

"We are playing really good baseball right now," Soto told MLB.com ahead of Friday's series opener with the Nationals. "Why not try to rejoin this team? It would be really fun. It would be great for me and the team. [I want to] finish the season strong and keep the momentum for next year, too."

Entering play Friday, the Mets are 5-3 since the Aug. 3 trade deadline and are getting major contributions from the young kids and some recent call-ups.

But New York could use an infusion of Soto. Before this latest injury, Soto was having a Soto-like season. However, being available has been a challenge for Soto. The slugger has missed 38 games entering Friday between his first stint on the IL with a right calf strain and this current injury to his left leg.

Soto called his 2026 injuries "tough" and hopes to learn from this experience and stay healthy for his team moving forward.

"It's tough for me to lose so many games. I've never been on this side of it," Soto said. "I think it's good for me -- for my career -- because it will teach me a lot of things. I have to adjust in my training [and] conditioning to keep moving forward in a positive way. I have to learn about my body a little bit more, learning how it works and go from there."

In 84 games this season, Soto has slashed .283/.408/.539 with 21 home runs and 52 RBI en route to another All-Star Game selection.

And while the Mets have yet to give a timeline for Soto's return, the outfielder was doing pregame workouts at Citi Field, in good spirits.

title: IndyCar President Doug Boles Furious About Safety At Markham
description: IndyCar Series President Doug Boles was strongly dissatisfied that the street course in Markham, Ontario was not completed and all Friday track action was cancelled.
fullText:
In what could have been a great opening day for IndyCar on the streets of Markham, Ontario turned into bitter disappointment for the huge throng of fans in the grandstands and for IndyCar President Doug Boles.

Instead of racing action, the only wheels turned on the 2.19-mile, 12-turn road course was construction machinery still trying to complete the track build. Without enough key tire packs in place to make for a safe impact area, IndyCar officials cancelled all track activity on Friday and issued a revised schedule for Saturday.

That left Boles furious that the track was not ready in time by the promoter of this weekend's event, and a key, longtime IndyCar ally, Green Savoree Promotions.

"IndyCar is incredibly disappointed that our promoter was not able to complete the track build on time, despite significant support from our team on site," Boles said. "Ontario has always been a magnificent market for our sport and the number of spectators that attended today is a shining example of that. New events can always pose logistical challenges and we join in the frustration of our loyal fans and apologize.

"Once we hit the track, we believe the circuit will be spectacular. We would like to thank the city of Markham for the major support it has made to provide IndyCar a layout, which is fast, technical and will put on a terrific show on Sunday."

There was a lot of excitement heading into the NTT IndyCar race at a new venue Friday on the streets of Markham, Ontario. The fans arrived early and filled the impressive grandstands, excited to witness IndyCar action in the buildup to Sunday's Ontario Honda Dealers Indy At Markham.

But the track wasn't ready and had some serious safety issues, including the lack of tire packs that are used as key safety barriers on street courses. They are needed for runoff areas and a few other places on track. The promoter had a plan in place to address that issue in time for Saturday morning's activity, according to IndyCar.

Other issues included a delay in the track build that included completing a full race track wall and fencing and significant safety concerns with areas of the wall and runoff.

Also, a lack of personnel to complete the tire and fence/wall construction.

The track build for the 2.19-mile, 12-turn street course race in Markham, Ontario began on July 19. The course is on the site of a GO Train station, which is still in use but the parking lots are the location of the double pit lane being used by INDYCAR. The parking lots closest to the pit lane were fully turned over to race promoters Green Savoree Promotions at end of day on Wednesday, August 12.

IndyCar continues to monitor the ongoing circuit construction by Green Savoree Racing Promotions.

IndyCar's Saturday schedule includes Practice 1 from 10-11:30 a.m. Eastern Time, televised on FS2, IndyCar Practice 2 from 2:30 to 4 p.m. on FS1 and Qualifying from 6:30 to 7 p.m. ET on FOX One, and 7-8 p.m. on FS2.

Because of time constraints in the early evening, IndyCar Series qualifying on Saturday will be in its traditional "road course" knockout qualifying format that will culminate with the "Firestone Fast Six" and the battle for the NTT P1 Award.
